anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 task is a static 5x5x3 isometric pile: the agent rotates among four views, ray-clicks exposed faces, removes blockers, extracts four directly exposed diamonds, avoids visible lava and fragile support, and explicitly exits. Its changes are discrete voxel removals and its grader replays rotations and clicks. Cloudpost d4 instead advances a plane every 40 ms through five procedural seals, requiring persistent two-axis heading correction, perspective/frustum search, and world-space contact within radius 12. Cloudpost has fewer explicit hazards and no voxel occlusion, but its continuing 3D control and contact timing are a materially broader control problem than the static L1 mine.

evidence.explanation: The approved baseline is L1/simplified and includes four targets, visible lava/support, and a limited-durability tool.
The visible mine uses discrete rotation events and canvas ray-mine events whose material outcome changes the pile, durability, inventory, and collapse state.
The approved grader independently replays the camera, click-ray occlusion, material, durability, and extraction state.
Cloudpost advances and contacts targets from a continuously moving 3D plane, with corridor failure when the plane leaves bounds.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 board has three ordered lamps, three walls, three wells, a momentum-bearing ball, and full analog tilt control with collision and hazard reset. Cloudpost d3 is comparable in having moderate closed-loop physical control and multiple milestones, while adding depth, perspective, and two angular axes. Cloudpost lacks the board's walls, wells, velocity momentum, and explicit recovery, so d3 is not automatically above L3; d4's tighter radius, faster flight, five seals, and longer ongoing correction burden provide the source-supported step toward L4.

evidence.explanation: The approved L3 baseline is full/live with three lamps, three walls, three hazards, and 50-ms board physics.
The approved generator activates ordered switches, walls, wells, and acceleration/friction/maximum-speed/bounce/ball-radius parameters.
The visible board runs deterministic physics with velocity, collisions, well reset, ordered lamp activation, and a goal cup.
The approved grader binds the interaction source and replays each tilt, physics tick, collision, hazard reset, ordered lamp, and completion state.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 candy task is a 5x5 changing-board search: four valid adjacent swaps must reach an exact score, each accepted swap changes the board and refill cursor through cascades, only five future candies are previewed, and black licorice voids the receipt. Cloudpost d5 has a higher continuous motor-control burden than d4, but collecting a seal only marks it collected and does not change future route physics or available actions. Cloudpost d5 can occupy the L5 band for precision and sustained control while remaining below this L5 anchor in state-dependent combinatorial planning.

evidence.explanation: The approved baseline is L5/simplified with a four-valid-swap exact-score requirement, at least seven waves, one forbidden candy, and a five-item preview.
The approved generator enumerates routes over successive boards and refill cursors, so each valid swap supplies a different later decision state.
The visible UI swaps candies, resolves repeated waves and refills, updates exact score, and terminates on exact change, overpayment, or move-budget exhaustion.
The approved grader replays each swap and cascade and requires exact score, move budget, wave threshold, and untouched licorice.
Cloudpost contact only adds an ID to the collected set; the plane physics and corridor checks remain the same.

visible_baseline_solution: At d4/full, the screenshot-only agent sees the prompt, a 0/5 seal counter, a flight tick, the 3D canvas with a fixed plane/cockpit marker, projected seals only when in the camera-frustum window, decorative scenery, a pointer crosshair, and HUD text stating that contact is world-space rather than screen overlap. It moves the pointer over the flight field to set a normalized yaw/pitch vector; that command persists until corrected and the plane advances on 40-ms ticks. The agent must use recent frames to find seals that may be outside view, steer toward their changing projected position and depth, keep the plane in the corridor, and bring the plane within 12 world units of all five seals. There is no manual submit: contacts auto-submit a replay ledger; corridor exit fails and issues a fresh route. Coordinates used by the private solver are implementation evidence, not information available to a policy-compliant screenshot-only solution.

baseline_judgment.rationale: Keep d4 as a provisional L4 assignment. It is above the static discrete L1 Isometric Voxel Extraction Mine because the plane continuously advances in 3D and requires repeated two-axis visual correction. It is above the approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board in depth/frustum reasoning and two-axis flight control, while lacking that anchor's walls, wells, momentum, and hazard resets. It is close to an L4 burden in milestone count and closed-loop correction, and below Exact-Change Candy Cascade L5 in state-dependent planning. The assignment is source-based rather than empirical calibration.

findings.claim: The simplified visible surface exposes only a coarse button-reachable control lattice, but the independent grader accepts arbitrary finite normalized vectors when a steer event is labeled trim_button.
findings.causal_explanation: The simplified handlers change yaw by fixed +/-0.12 increments, pitch by fixed +/-0.10 increments, or reset to zero; the full handler maps any pointer position to a continuous normalized pair. The grader checks the expected input_source and clamps the submitted pair to [-1, 1], but does not validate the simplified value set or transition sequence. A direct result payload with hidden implementation access could therefore label continuous controls as trim_button. The opposite full/simplified source transcript is rejected, and this does not prove that a policy-compliant screenshot-only agent can exploit it, but it weakens the selected-surface contract and leaves the material completion-rate effect uncertain.

evidence.explanation: The simplified control function changes the persistent vector by fixed deltas and records trim_button.
The visible simplified UI binds fixed trim actions, while full interaction binds canvas pointermove.
The grader selects the expected source and clamps arbitrary submitted values without checking button-reachable values or transitions.
The source test covers opposite-source rejection but not the simplified numeric lattice; it was not run here.

findings.recommended_action: If strict input-surface binding is required, enforce the simplified handler's reachable values and transitions in the independent grader. A separate permitted multi-seed/runtime check should measure whether coarse control materially changes route feasibility before changing difficulty labels.

concise_summary: Keep Cloudpost Circuit at the provisional L4/full baseline. Its active d1-d5 profiles form an ordered 3D control ladder; d4 is above the approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board in perspective and sustained flight control but below the approved L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade in changing-state planning. The simplified interaction has a source-proven grader/input-domain qualification.
limitations: This was source-only analysis. No generator, browser, grader, exported verifier, human, or computer-use-agent run was performed. Multi-seed route reachability, completion/timing distributions, and the effect of simplified command quantization remain uncalibrated. No historical pre-controls implementation was supplied.
